text:
John Tavares missed nine games with a lower-body injury from mid-October, and since he returned against Montreal on Nov. 7 the Maple Leafs have not won. He has no points in five games back, and our numbers do not call that slump due on his own shots: the chances have thinned out too.

The bigger worry is the minutes he is on the ice for. Toronto gets just 35.86% of expected goals at 5v5 with the 36-year-old on, 12.52 points worse than when he sits. Some of that is luck going the wrong way (the Leafs have scored 6.1 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him out there), and Evolving-Hockey had him playing with weak teammates against strong competition last season. Some of it is a team shuffling lines; the Leafs called up Ryan Tverberg to play beside him and William Nylander.

There is plenty in the tank by the evidence. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him 98th percentile for chances from the home-plate area last season, and his own shots this season are still worth 1.1 expected goals per 60. The goals have not followed yet, and the Leafs need them to.
headline: John Tavares came back to a team in a skid
